defect: Directory capture validated and pinned an opened Windows target handle but then enumerated the original path using QDirIterator. An allowed in-mount junction alias could be retargeted without renaming the pinned target. Shallow/preview listing then exposed filenames from a separate outside fixture.
test_mechanism: The test translation unit includes the actual ToolExecutor.cpp with local CreateFileW/GetFinalPathNameByHandleW wrappers. Windows headers are included first, so the wrappers call the original APIs. Only the controlled FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY fixture handle triggers mutation, immediately after the final canonical path buffer is filled. Production has no test hook or altered authority.

before.source: Private reconstruction of the reviewed old captureDirectory helper inside the current asynchronous adapter; not an earlier Git commit.
before.observed: Shallow ls and directory preview returned OUTSIDE_ROOT_MARKER.txt. Recursive ls and full directory read failed after child path validation detected the retargeted alias. The four tests require the originally validated directory to remain readable with no outside marker.

fix: Windows captureDirectory now enumerates FILE_ID_BOTH_DIR_INFO records from the validated handle using GetFileInformationByHandleEx. Recursive opens use the validated canonical directory path plus each contained child name and validate a fresh child handle. File contents already use same-handle scoped reads. Formatted captures execute on QtConcurrent with immutable arguments, a shared atomic cancellation flag and a context-owned QFutureWatcher.

cases: Shallow/recursive ls and full/preview directory read retain owned markers after alias retargeting
Cancel while the actual worker is held at an opened directory boundary yields only the cancellation
A replacement using the same request ID completes while the obsolete worker remains held and receives no stale completion after release
Destroying ToolExecutor while held returns promptly; its storage is changed to PAGE_NOACCESS before the worker resumes and completes without accessing it

limits: All path mutation was confined to owned temporary fixtures. The held-worker tests establish the tested cancellation/destruction boundaries; they do not prove universal filesystem race freedom or bounded latency of arbitrary operating-system calls. Parent integrated suite results and later source revisions are tracked separately.
